definitions.gloss: to demolish; to tear down; to pull down
definitions.explanation: To deliberately destroy a building or structure, typically as part of a planned demolition or redevelopment. A compound verb formed from 取り (taking action) + 壊す (to break/destroy).

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{家|いえ}を{取|と}り{壊|こわ}す。
examples.english: To tear down an old house.

examples.japanese: あのビルは{来月|らいげつ}{取|と}り{壊|こわ}される{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: That building is scheduled to be demolished next month.

examples.japanese: {歴史的|れきしてき}な{建物|たてもの}を{取|と}り{壊|こわ}すことに{反対|はんたい}する{住民|じゅうみん}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many residents oppose demolishing the historic building.

notes:
USAGE:
{取|と}り{壊|こわ}す is used for planned, deliberate demolition of structures. The passive form {取|と}り{壊|こわ}される is very common in news and announcements about buildings being torn down.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {建物|たてもの}を{取|と}り{壊|こわ}す (demolish a building)
- {家|いえ}を{取|と}り{壊|こわ}す (tear down a house)
- {取|と}り{壊|こわ}し{工事|こうじ} (demolition work)
- {取|と}り{壊|こわ}し{予定|よてい} (scheduled for demolition)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{解体|かいたい}する is a more formal/technical term for demolition or dismantling. {壊|こわ}す alone means "to break" or "to destroy" but doesn't specifically imply systematic demolition of a structure.
